entries.title: Isaiah 15:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The burden - A prophecy of the destruction of the Moabites, the inveterate enemies of the Jews, begun by the Assyrian, and finished by the Babylonian emperors. In a night - Suddenly and unexpectedly. Ar - The chief city of Moab. Kir - Another eminent city of Moab.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bajith - Which signifies an house. It is supposed to be some eminent house or temple of their idols. Dibon - Another city of Moab. To weep - To offer their supplications with tears to their idols for help. Medeba - Two considerable cities, anciently belonging to the Moabites. Beard - The hair of their heads and beards was shaved, as was usual in great mournings.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: On the tops - Which were made flat, to which men used to go up, to cry to God in heaven, or to men for help.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Heshbon - Two other Moabitish cities. Jahaz - Another city in the utmost borders of Moab. Soldiers - Who use to be the most courageous.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Moab - Tho' they are a most vile nation. Zoar - Zoar was a town bordering upon Moab. Of destruction - Such a cry as men send forth when they are just falling into the pit of destruction.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Waters - Watery grounds being very fruitful, are commonly most inhabited; but now they also, much more the dry and barren grounds, shall be desolate and without inhabitant.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They - Their enemies. Brook - Possibly he means some such river which ran into Euphrates, and so gave them opportunity of carrying their spoils by water unto Babylon.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The cry - Their cry fills all the parts of the country.

entries.title: Isaiah 15:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: More - More than hath been already mentioned. Lions - God shall send lions to find out those that escape the fury of men.
